topics.title: Styling in React: Four Methods
topics.keyConcept: React supports multiple styling strategies: Inline styles, standard CSS stylesheets, scoped CSS Modules, and dynamic CSS-in-JS (styled-components).
topics.content:
Styling components in React goes beyond traditional stylesheets. The four main styling methods are compared below:

MethodScopeDynamic SupportBuild-time OverheadSyntax Style
Inline StylesComponent-scopedHigh (reads JS variables)NoneJS Style Objects
Standard CSSGlobal (affects whole DOM)Low (requires class toggling)NoneCSS Stylesheets
CSS ModulesLocally Scoped (unique hash)Low (class mapping)Low (build compilation)CSS Stylesheets
Styled-ComponentsLocally ScopedVery High (reads props)High (runtime CSS parsing)Tagged Template Literals

Code Examples (CSS Modules vs. Styled-Components):

Using **CSS Modules** (Button.module.css):

// CSS File: .btnPrimary { background: black; color: white; }

// JSX File:
import styles from './Button.module.css';
const Button = () => <button className={styles.btnPrimary}>Click</button>;

Using **Styled-Components**:

import styled from 'styled-components';
const StyledBtn = styled.button`
  background: ${props => props.primary ? 'black' : 'white'};
  color: ${props => props.primary ? 'white' : 'black'};
`;
const App = () => <StyledBtn primary>Dynamic Button</StyledBtn>;
topics.commonMistakes: Assuming CSS files imported standardly inside a component are scoped to that component. Writing `import './Button.css';` inside `Button.jsx` actually loads those classes globally. If another component has identical class names, styling conflicts will occur. Use CSS Modules to prevent this.
topics.interviewTip: Expect questions on CSS Modules vs. Styled-Components. Emphasize that CSS Modules are scoped statically at build time, while styled-components are dynamic (they can read component props to alter styles dynamically at runtime).

topics.title: Bootstrap & React Tables
topics.keyConcept: Bootstrap in React can be loaded via CDN or imported as native React-Bootstrap components. Dynamic tables render data arrays using .map().
topics.content:
Integrating CSS frameworks like Bootstrap speeds up development:

  • React-Bootstrap: A library that rebuilds Bootstrap components from scratch as React components. Instead of writing class strings, you import elements directly: 
    import { Button, Table } from 'react-bootstrap';
const el = <Button variant="dark">Bootstrap Button</Button>;
  • Rendering Dynamic Lists: Tabular data is rendered in React by mapping over arrays inside the JSX layout. You must always assign a unique key prop to the outer row element to help React track which items changed, added, or removed.
const userList = [
  { id: 101, name: 'Aritra', grade: 'A' },
  { id: 102, name: 'Rahul', grade: 'B' }
];

const UserTable = () => (
  <table className="table">
    <tbody>
      {userList.map(user => (
        <tr key={user.id}>
          <td>{user.name}</td>
          <td>{user.grade}</td>
        </tr>
      ))}
    </tbody>
  </table>
);
topics.commonMistakes: Forgetting to provide a unique `key` prop, or using array indices (`index`) as keys. If the array is reordered or filtered, using index keys can lead to rendering issues and state bugs.

topics.title: React Router (Client-side Routing)
topics.keyConcept: React Router enables client-side SPA routing by matching URL paths to components and intercepting page reloads using Link and useNavigate.
topics.content:
React Router is the standard routing library for React SPAs. It synchronizes the UI with the browser URL. Key components and hooks in **React Router v6** include:

  • BrowserRouter: A wrapper component that provides history and URL routing context to the application.
  • Routes: A container component that matches the current browser location against child Route definitions.
  • Route: Maps a specific path to a component: <Route path="/contact" element={<Contact />} />.
  • Link: Generates clickable navigation links. It replaces anchor tags to prevent browser reloads.
  • useNavigate: A hook that returns a function for programmatic navigation (e.g., redirecting users after login).

React Router v6 Code Example:

import { BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, Link, useNavigate } from 'react-router-dom';

const Home = () => <h1>Home View</h1>;
const Dashboard = () => {
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  return (
    <div>
      <h1>Dashboard</h1>
      <button onClick={() => navigate('/')}>Logout Programmatically</button>
    </div>
  );
};

const App = () => (
  <BrowserRouter>
    <nav>
      <Link to="/">Home</Link> | <Link to="/dashboard">Dashboard</Link>
    </nav>
    <Routes>
      <Route path="/" element={<Home />} />
      <Route path="/dashboard" element={<Dashboard />} />
    </Routes>
  </BrowserRouter>
);
topics.commonMistakes: Using standard `<a href="/dashboard">` links instead of React Router's `<Link to="/dashboard">`. Standard anchor tags cause the browser to perform a full page reload, wiping out the application state and defeating the purpose of an SPA.

topics.title: Props & Type Validation
topics.keyConcept: Props are read-only inputs passed from parents to children. Prop-types is a runtime type-checking system that alerts developers to validation issues.
topics.content:
Props (short for properties) are read-only configuration attributes passed down a component tree. Props are immutable inside the receiver component.

Prop-Types Validation: In JavaScript, React cannot enforce parameter types. To prevent runtime type bugs, developers use the prop-types library. This runs checks on props during development, emitting console warnings if mismatched values are passed.

import PropTypes from 'prop-types';

const UserCard = ({ name, age, isActive }) => (
  <div className="card">
    <h3>{name}</h3>
    <p>Age: {age}</p>
    <span>Status: {isActive ? 'Active' : 'Offline'}</span>
  </div>
);

UserCard.propTypes = {
  name: PropTypes.string.isRequired, // Triggers error if missing
  age: PropTypes.number,
  isActive: PropTypes.bool.isRequired
};

UserCard.defaultProps = {
  age: 18 // Default value if prop is omitted
};
topics.commonMistakes: Modifying props inside a child component (e.g. attempting `props.name = 'John'`). Props are strictly read-only. If you need to change a value, manage it as state inside the parent component and pass a callback modifier down.

topics.title: React State Concepts
topics.keyConcept: State is component-local, changeable data that triggers component re-rendering. State updates are batched and scheduled asynchronously.
topics.content:
State represents dynamic data managed internally by a component. When state changes, React automatically re-renders the component and its children to synchronize the UI.

Core Rules of React State:

  1. Treat State as Immutable: Never mutate state directly. Doing state.count++ will not trigger React's diffing engine. Always call the setter function (setCount(prev => prev + 1)).
  2. State Updates are Asynchronous: React batches multiple state changes into a single re-render cycle for performance. Thus, reading state directly after setting it might return the old value: 
    // MISTAKE:
setCount(count + 1);
console.log(count); // Prints old value

// CORRECT (using functional update):
setCount(prev => prev + 1);

Real-World Project Example: Search bars. The query input field is mapped to a local state variable `searchQuery`. On every keystroke, the `onChange` event updates the state, triggering a re-render of filtered results.
topics.commonMistakes: Writing complex object updates incorrectly. For example: `setProfile({ name: 'John' })` on a state containing `{ name: 'Alice', age: 25 }` will wipe out the `age` property. In functional state setters, you must copy the old fields: `setProfile(prev => ({ ...prev, name: 'John' }))`.

practiceQuestions.question: How do inline styles differ in React compared to standard HTML?
practiceQuestions.answer: In standard HTML, styles are written as semi-colon separated strings. In React, inline styles are written as JavaScript objects where property names are camelCased (e.g., `fontSize` instead of `font-size`) and values are strings (e.g., `color: 'blue'`).

practiceQuestions.question: What are CSS Modules and what problem do they solve in React?
practiceQuestions.answer: CSS Modules are CSS files where all class names are scoped locally by default. They solve the problem of global namespace pollution and naming conflicts in large React projects, ensuring that styling in one component does not leak and affect other components.

practiceQuestions.question: Describe the main routing components in React Router and their purposes.
practiceQuestions.answer: (1) `BrowserRouter`: Connects the app to the browser URL. (2) `Routes`: Matches the current URL path against route definitions. (3) `Route`: Maps a specific path to a React component. (4) `Link`: Creates client-side navigation links that prevent browser page reloads.

practiceQuestions.question: How do you perform props validation in React? Provide a code snippet.
Explain the key rules regarding updating state in React.
practiceQuestions.answer: (1) Do not mutate state directly; always use the state setter function (`setState` or the hook returned setter). (2) State updates are scheduled and may be asynchronous. (3) Always treat state as immutable when updating complex objects (use spreading: `setObj({...obj, key: val})`).

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the correct syntax for writing inline styles in React?
mcqs.explanation: React inline styles are passed as JS objects within JSX brackets, requiring camelCased styling attributes.

mcqs.question: What is the benefit of using CSS Modules in React?
options: They make styling run faster on servers
They scope class names locally by default, avoiding global styling clashes
They translate CSS code to Python
mcqs.explanation: CSS Modules compile class names into unique hashes, ensuring styles remain scoped only to their specific importing component.

mcqs.question: In React Router, which component is used to define navigation paths instead of standard <a> tags?
mcqs.explanation: The Link component intercepts browser clicks and updates history locally without causing page refreshes.

mcqs.question: How do you specify that a component prop is mandatory using PropTypes?
mcqs.explanation: Appending `.isRequired` to any PropTypes type check raises warnings in the browser console if that prop is omitted.

mcqs.question: Why should you never modify component state directly (e.g. state.count = 5)?
options: It bypasses React's virtual DOM trigger, failing to re-render the UI
mcqs.explanation: React detects state changes by intercepting setter calls. Modifying state properties directly does not schedule re-renders.

mcqs.question: In React Router, which component acts as a container for all Route declarations?
mcqs.explanation: In React Router v6, the `<Routes>` component wraps individual `<Route>` components to select the best match.

mcqs.question: Which CSS-in-JS library allows writing actual CSS within your component code?
mcqs.explanation: styled-components uses tagged template literals to build React components with attached styling rules.

mcqs.question: How do we render list rows dynamically in a table component?
options: Using a for loop in JSX
Using the array .map() method to return row elements
Using a while loop inside brackets
mcqs.explanation: The standard React approach is iterating arrays using `.map()` and returning the JSX structure for each row element.

mcqs.question: When updating state based on the previous state, which method is safest?
options: Passing a callback function to the state setter: (prev) => prev + 1
mcqs.explanation: Since state updates are batched, passing a callback ensures you receive the most current, up-to-date state values.

mcqs.question: Which prop-types category is used to check for an array of a specific type?
mcqs.explanation: Use `PropTypes.arrayOf(PropTypes.type)` to enforce that an array only contains elements of a matching target type.
